summary: This week's GCC developments reflect an accelerating integration of artificial intelligence across government and financial services, alongside significant cross-border capital mobilisation. The UAE reinforced its regional leadership in technology adoption, highlighted by reports indicating a 70.1% AI usage rate and targeted ecosystem engagement, including a delegation of Emirati AI experts exploring China's market. Meanwhile, financial and regulatory updates underscored structural developments, such as SoftBank's pursuit of up to $100 billion from Gulf investors for new AI initiatives, Kuwait's introduction of the first domestic Buy Now, Pay Later service via KIB, and Oman's Muscat Stock Exchange entering the FTSE Russell watchlist. Public sector digital transformation also advanced, with Qatar preparing an AI-powered National Legal Knowledge Platform and Bahrain's National Bank of Bahrain expanding enterprise AI adoption through its AI@NBB initiative. For C-suite executives, these trends demonstrate a maturing technological landscape where institutional AI implementation and international capital deployment require robust governance, strategic alignment, and proactive risk management to maintain competitive advantage across the region.

stories.t: SoftBank seeks up to $100bln from Gulf investors for new AI push
stories.b: SoftBank's CEO is reportedly seeking between $50 billion and $100 billion from Gulf investors to fund a major new artificial intelligence expansion.
stories.w: This capital raising highlights the Gulf's growing role as the primary financial backer for global AI infrastructure and venture scaling, with direct implications for regional sovereign investment strategy.

stories.t: UAE leads world in AI adoption with 70.1% usage rate, Microsoft report says
stories.b: A newly released Microsoft report indicates that the UAE has achieved a 70.1% AI usage rate, positioning it as a global leader in national technology adoption.
stories.w: It sets a benchmark for enterprise digital maturity in the region, validating national transformation strategies and raising consumer and corporate expectations for AI-enabled services.

stories.t: KIB launches BuyNow, first BNPL service by a Kuwaiti bank
stories.b: Kuwait International Bank (KIB) has introduced 'BuyNow', marking the first Buy Now, Pay Later financial service offered directly by a domestic Kuwaiti bank.
stories.w: Traditional banks are increasingly encroaching on fintech territory to capture tech-savvy retail segments and modernize consumer lending portfolios.

stories.t: Muscat Stock Exchange Added to FTSE Russell Watchlist
stories.b: The Muscat Stock Exchange has officially been added to the FTSE Russell watchlist, marking a crucial step toward potential classification upgrades.
stories.w: Inclusion on international watchlists enhances market visibility, paving the way for increased institutional portfolio inflows and higher governance standards for listed Omani entities.

stories.t: Qatar's MoJ to Launch AI-powered National Legal Knowledge Platform
stories.b: Qatar's Ministry of Justice announced the upcoming launch of an artificial intelligence-driven National Legal Knowledge Platform to streamline legal research and services.
stories.w: Demonstrates public sector momentum in deploying vertical-specific AI tools to optimize internal government operations and enhance public service delivery.

stories.t: NBB Advances Enterprise AI Transformation Through AI@NBB
stories.b: The National Bank of Bahrain (NBB) is accelerating its institutional adoption of artificial intelligence through the structured rollout of its internal AI@NBB framework.
stories.w: Highlights how regional financial institutions are systematically embedding artificial intelligence into core operational workflows rather than treating it as a peripheral technology.

stories.t: BENEFIT announces NBB as first bank to join Bahrain’s Trade Finance Registry project
stories.b: BENEFIT has announced that the National Bank of Bahrain has become the first financial institution to join Bahrain's newly established Trade Finance Registry project.
stories.w: Collaborative infrastructure initiatives like trade registries reduce institutional risk, curb duplicate financing fraud, and improve transparency across regional banking systems.

stories.t: 16 Emirati AI experts to explore China’s AI ecosystem
stories.b: A delegation of sixteen Emirati artificial intelligence experts has embarked on an exploratory visit to study and engage with China's broader AI technology ecosystem.
stories.w: Reflects the UAE's outward-looking technology policy, fostering cross-border R&D partnerships and sourcing alternative global frameworks for domestic deployment.

stories.t: Have a money-smart idea? UAE Central Bank wants to hear from you
stories.b: The Central Bank of the UAE has launched an initiative inviting public and industry participation to submit innovative financial technology and consumer finance ideas.
stories.w: Encourages open innovation channels between regulators and market participants, supporting regulatory sandbox pipelines and early-stage fintech concepts.

stories.t: Google to restrict free access to Gemini AI models
stories.b: Industry reports indicate that Google is planning to introduce restrictions on free public access to its Gemini artificial intelligence models.
stories.w: Signals a broader commercial shift in the generative AI market toward enterprise monetization, forcing organizations to budget for enterprise-grade API licenses.

themes.b: Financial institutions and government bodies across the GCC are rapidly operationalizing internal artificial intelligence frameworks, moving from pilot phases to enterprise-wide deployments. Examples include NBB's AI@NBB initiative in Bahrain, Qatar's new legal knowledge platform, and high reported national usage rates in the UAE.

Regional entities continue to forge strategic international alliances, underscored by SoftBank seeking up to $100 billion from Gulf investors and Emirati AI delegations engaging directly with foreign technology markets like China to secure technological edge and investment returns.

Regulators and exchanges are actively upgrading domestic market structures—highlighted by Oman's MSX watchlist inclusion, Kuwait's entry into bank-led BNPL services, and the UAE Central Bank's open innovation outreach—to boost transparency, competition, and investor inflows.

items: Audit existing enterprise AI tool deployments against emerging commercial pricing models following third-party vendor restrictions.
Evaluate infrastructure readiness to support large-scale internal AI frameworks inspired by regional peers like AI@NBB.
Engage with regional fintech and regulatory sandbox initiatives to identify prospective co-development partners for core banking upgrades.
Review data governance protocols for proprietary legal and financial datasets integrated into upcoming vertical AI platforms.
Assess third-party risk management frameworks concerning international software vendors and cross-border AI development tools.
Incorporate trade registry data-sharing security standards in alignment with new multi-institution registries like Bahrain's Trade Finance project.
Establish unified data taxonomy standards to support enterprise-wide AI transformation programs and automated grading or processing assistants.
Prepare institutional datasets for seamless integration into national knowledge platforms and regulatory reporting registries.
Monitor data privacy compliance as retail banking entities expand digital lending and alternative credit scoring models like BNPL.
Align internal workforce upskilling programs with high national AI adoption benchmarks observed across the UAE market.
Incorporate international benchmark criteria, such as FTSE Russell watchlist inclusion standards, into long-term corporate roadmaps.
Design change management strategies to support the shift from experimental AI pilots to mandatory enterprise-grade operational platforms.

market.b: High enterprise adoption rates across the UAE and proactive institutional rollouts in Bahrain and Qatar highlight a maturing market moving toward commercial monetization and specialized vertical deployment.
Regional banks are actively diversifying product offerings through bank-backed BNPL products in Kuwait and trade registry integrations in Bahrain to capture new segments and reduce counterparty risk.
Public sector entities are prioritizing knowledge management and administrative automation, leveraging AI platforms to streamline legal frameworks and educational evaluation processes.
Oman's inclusion on the FTSE Russell watchlist reflects positive structural progress in regional exchange governance and institutional investor attractiveness.

ceo.lead: If I were advising the CEO of a Gulf bank or government technology organisation, the three issues I would put on the leadership agenda this week are...
items: Capitalizing on global AI investment trends while establishing clear internal governance frameworks to manage vendor cost shifts and enterprise licensing changes.
Accelerating internal enterprise AI transformation roadmaps to keep pace with soaring national adoption rates and peer benchmarks in the UAE and Bahrain.
Preparing organizational infrastructure for heightened capital market scrutiny and regulatory modernization, exemplified by exchange watchlist developments and new trade finance registries.
